description:
Build or reorganise the whole agent org chart in ONE call — create departments and place agents into them atomically.

HOW TO USE THIS WELL:
1. Call get_org_chart first to see every agent, its description, and any existing groups.
2. Read the agent NAMES and DESCRIPTIONS and group them by what they actually do — engineering, design, research, content, quality, and so on. Use the user's own vocabulary where their agents suggest one; do not force a generic taxonomy onto a workspace that clearly has a different shape.
3. Put genuinely shared utility agents (ones used across many workflows, e.g. a Planner or Reviewer) in their own group rather than scattering them.
4. Send every department and placement in a single apply_org_plan call. Do NOT loop one agent at a time.

IMPORTANT — LEAVE context EMPTY on this call unless the user has already told you what a group's standards are. A department with empty context inherits nothing, so grouping changes how agents are ORGANISED without changing how any of them BEHAVE. That is what makes it safe to propose a whole structure unprompted. Silently inventing standards rewrites how the user's agents work, which is not yours to decide.

THEN OFFER TO FILL THEM IN — this is the step that makes the org do anything. After applying the grouping, say so plainly: the groups are empty, so nothing has changed yet. Offer to draft the standards for each one, and use manage_org action=set_context once they agree.

WHAT GOOD DEPARTMENT CONTEXT LOOKS LIKE — the instruction the user would otherwise repeat to every agent in the group. Draft it from what you can actually observe (their agents' existing prompts, their libraries, how they talk to you), then show it and let them correct it. Never present a guess as their standard.
  Engineering — stack and conventions; definition of done; what must never change without asking
  Design      — which design system; states every screen must cover; the accessibility bar
  Content     — voice and tone; spelling convention; words and claims to avoid
  Research    — what counts as a source; how to separate fact from speculation; citation format
  Delivery    — definition of done; when to escalate; how to hand work to the next agent
  A squad or project group — what we are building; who it is for; what is out of scope

Departments are matched by name, case-insensitively — reusing an existing name updates it instead of creating a duplicate. Placements are additive by default; pass replaceExisting: true to move agents that already sit somewhere else.

Tell the user what you grouped and why, and mention they can drag anything afterwards or clear the whole thing to start over.

departments.description: Departments to create or reuse. Existing names are reused, not duplicated.

context.description: Shared standards inherited by every agent beneath. LEAVE EMPTY unless the user specified them.

description.description: Why this group exists — shown to the user.

handoffs.description: Optional non-inheriting links between agents that work together. No context passes along these.

placements.description: Which agent goes in which department. Department must appear in `departments` or already exist.

replaceExisting.description: Move agents that already have a parent. Default false (only place unplaced agents).

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID. Defaults to your active workspace.

name: apply_org_plan
